direction: [A bubbly nine-year-old kid, fast, bright and energetic, telling a friend an amazing story; not whispery, breathy or soft]
lines: Grandpa has saved our village from thirty-one raids.
Every single one started the night he came home.
Grandpa said, "They know who beats them."
When he walks by, the villagers throw him bread.
He hunts at the old tower on the hill.
He brings back grey bottles. He's got a whole chest.
He calls it his courage. He drinks it at the gate.
Since Grandma died a raid is the only time anyone's glad to see him.
Tonight, he came home too tired to fight.
So I drank his courage. Somebody had to fight.
Lock the door, kid. They're coming.
Now they'll love you too, kid.
